title: Littoral invertebrate richness in 109 Swedish lakes rose in 1995-2022 only through label changes and chironomid genera; family richness did not rise, and lake trends did not follow local warming
abstract: A 2025 study of 110 Swedish monitoring lakes reported that littoral macroinvertebrate taxon richness increased (45 significant increases, 5 decreases, +1.6% per year) and related this to climate. We used the same public CC0 data (1995-2022) and audited taxonomic labels and sample size. We merged labels to genus and family with the GBIF backbone and merged three groups whose names changed. The published result reproduced exactly at label level. At family level, 21 lakes increased and 14 decreased, and the median trend was zero. Label changes, which occurred mainly in 2003 and 2013, made 39% of the trend. Chironomid genera made 89% of the genus-level trend (+1.74 genera per lake per decade). Other genera (+0.22, CI -0.28 to 0.72) and families (+0.05, CI -0.27 to 0.42) did not increase. Individuals per sample increased by about 21% per decade. At fixed abundance, families and other genera decreased slightly. Lake trends did not follow lake trends in air or water temperature, pH, phosphorus or organic carbon. Chironomid genera increased in the north and south in 1995-2008 and 2009-2022, but profundal chironomid genera from the same laboratory decreased. The within-lake air-temperature link came only from chironomid genera, and it disappeared with year effects. Organic carbon (browning) had the most robust positive link. We found no evidence that pH recovery from acidification increased richness. Limitation: the tables give transformed abundances, not raw counts, so we could not rarefy, and we have no laboratory protocol history. A real change in chironomid assemblages remains possible, but the data cannot separate it from a change in sample processing.

Lower panel: summed lake share of labels that started (blue) or stopped (orange) in each year in the 82 long-record lakes. Dotted lines: main label-change years 2003, 2013 and 2017.

Within-lake richness trend per decade (95% lake bootstrap) for labels, all genera, chironomid genera, other genera and families, without (circles) and with (squares) log total abundance as a covariate.
Trends per decade north and south of about 60.5 N in 1995-2008 and 2009-2022. Chironomid genera increased in all four samples; families increased only in 1995-2008.

citations.reason: Original claim: littoral macroinvertebrate richness increased and tracked climate in these lakes. We reproduce the label-level counts and show that family-level and non-chironomid richness did not increase.
Source data (CC0): physicochemical, climate, littoral and profundal tables for 110 Swedish national monitoring lakes, 1992-2022.
